readme: Twelve worked items with the lineage a real campaign produces: two and three annotators per item, genuine disagreement, and one adjudication under each rule the protocol names including an escalation that resolves to nothing. The confusion table it produces is hand-computed in tests/test_calibration_metrics.py: 4 true passes, 2 false passes, 3 true fails, 1 false fail, 1 judge abstention and 1 unresolved reference. The judge decisions are PREDICTIONS; no judge has been run. Every rationale_ref and guideline_ref in this file is the sha256 of the content carried beside it, and the loader checks that, so editing a rationale without re-deriving its digest fails the load.

guideline.summary: Claim support: a claim is supported only when the cited source states it or entails it without a further assumption; contradicted when the source states the reverse; not_verifiable when no admissible evidence could settle it; abstain when the annotator cannot decide from the material shown. Rubric coverage: an item is covered when the report satisfies it with admissible evidence, and stating a genuine evidence gap satisfies the gap item. Never reward fluency, length, or confidence. Full guide: docs/agent-engineering/14-judge-calibration-protocol.md.

rationales.text: Both annotators found the claim stated verbatim in the cited abstract; the adjudicator confirmed without changing anything, which is what a unanimous adjudication records.
Two annotators found no entailment; the third read the source's related-work paragraph as the source's own finding. Majority rule applied and the minority decision is preserved above.

Two annotators found the claim entailed by the reported numbers; the third wanted an explicit sentence. Majority rule applied; the disagreement is about how much inference an annotator may do and is a guide follow-up.

The two annotators split between supported and unsupported. Reading both rationales, the adjudicating expert found the cited source states the reverse, which neither annotator had claimed, so the outcome is a third value and this record is why an override may leave the observed decisions.

One annotator called the claim unverifiable, one unsupported. Guide clause 4.2: when a source exists and is silent, the decision is unsupported; not_verifiable is reserved for claims no admissible source could settle.

Three annotators, three decisions, and the adjudicator could not resolve them from the material shown: the source excerpt is ambiguous about which experimental arm the number belongs to. Escalated. The item carries no reference decision and enters no denominator.
Both annotators found the claim stated in the cited abstract.
Both annotators found the claim entailed by a table the abstract summarises.
Both annotators found the claim supported by an explicit sentence.
Both annotators found the cited source silent on the claim's operative quantity.
Both annotators found the source reporting the opposite direction, which is contradicted rather than merely unsupported.
Both annotators found the rubric's evidence-gap item satisfied: the report names the missing measurement rather than substituting an adjacent one.
